A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Structured Initialization for Vision Transformers. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments, initialization comparisons, training-setting and ConvMixer ablations, and five-run statistical results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a ViT-Base training configuration and CIFAR-10 convergence results.

M1.justification: The impulse-based attention initialization, positional-encoding pseudo-input, SVD solution, normalization, and adaptations to Swin Transformer and MLP-Mixer remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image-classification coverage: Food-101, CIFAR-10/100, STL-10, Flowers, Pets, and ImageNet-1K, with the same ImageNet-21K pretraining comparison. The additions concern existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding initialization, weight-selection, and ConvMixer experiments. The added ViT-Base configuration and convergence analysis use the existing default and mimetic baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT-Base* using 16 V100 GPUs and color jitter of 0.3, plus CIFAR-10 evaluations at epochs 10, 50, and 100. Table 2 also adopts the learning-rate 1e-3/repeated-augmentation 3 configuration already present in v1's Table 5, replacing the headline 7e-4/1 configuration.

E4.justification: Section 5.3, Figure 3, and Appendix F.3 add CIFAR-10 convergence evidence, including early-epoch comparisons in Table 7. ImageNet training-curve analysis, learning-rate/augmentation ablations, and ConvMixer filter-size/width experiments already existed in v1 and remain.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.1 newly specifies different seeds and stochastic filter generation for the five runs. Five-run means, standard deviations, and error bars were already reported in v1 Appendix G.2/Figure 5 and remain in v2 Appendix F.2/Figure 6; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: New results include ViT-Base* accuracies of 81.89/80.56/82.13 for default/mimetic/impulse and CIFAR-10 checkpoint results, such as 76.87/77.64/81.87 at epoch 100. The ordinary ViT-Base values now in Table 2, 81.24/80.56/81.83, already appeared in v1 Table 5; they are not same-setting improvements over v1's headline results.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Proposition 1, its corollaries and proof, and the initialization and convolution-matrix derivations are unchanged. Appendix F.4 applies the existing filter-span argument to head counts without adding a formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: convolutional inductive bias through initialization without architectural modification, stronger small-data performance, preserved large-data flexibility, and applicability across architectures.

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a tentative explanation connecting initialization norms to convergence. F.4 links model-size benefits to attention-head counts and excludes larger ViTs on small datasets because of optimization instability. Its increasing-gain interpretation is not consistently supported by Table 2. The earlier limitations are relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies training from scratch and the absence of ImageNet pretraining or distillation, and documents the additional 16-GPU/color-jitter configuration. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments. The code URL is unchanged and merely moves to a footnote.

R1.justification: The 37 references and related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning against architectural CNN–ViT hybrids, pretrained-weight initialization, and earlier convolution–attention connections remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.3 and Appendix F.3–F.4, moves limitations from Appendix A into main-text Section 6, and revises experimental explanations. Affiliation, contact, and conference text also change. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel training-curve Figure 3, checkpoint Table 7, and a yellow-highlighted ViT-Base* column in Table 2. Existing attention maps, appendix plots, and the ConvMixer table are retained with relocation, resizing, or renumbering; Table 5 loses its old headline-row highlight.

improvement.justification: Promoting the stronger baseline already available in v1's appendix makes the main comparison more balanced. The additional ViT-Base setting, convergence evidence, and training clarifications provide modest gains in support and transparency. These gains are limited by stale augmentation wording in Appendix E and the insufficiently supported model-size interpretation in Appendix F.4.
